Subject: Follow-up: data handling items from today’s demo

Jake / Anna — thanks again for the 45‑minute demo this morning. Quick recap and the items you asked us to follow up on: 

Summary of TerraHeal asks from today
- Types of data sent to the model: PII (name, phone, user health metadata) and device telemetry.
- Data residency: primary requirement is EU residency for PHI-adjacent telemetry; fallback US ok for dev.
- Retention: default short-term logs + ability to retain raw telemetry for 90 days for audit.
- Logging / evidence: need requestable audit logs that do not expose raw PII, plus ability to export redacted logs for incident review.
- DPA items: explicit controller/processor mapping, subprocessors list, breach-notice SLAs (TerraHeal prefers 48 hours).

Requests / next steps
1) Could you confirm the exact retention target (30/60/90 days) you require for production vs. staging?
2) I’ve attached a short checklist (redwood-data-questions-brief.pdf) with specific DPA clauses you highlighted — please add any missing items and return.
3) We’ll pull our subprocessor list and an incident-notification proposal; legal will propose language for the controller/processor section.

Target timeline
- I’ll get a first-pass response from legal + infra by EOD Dec 7 so you have language to review before next week’s procurement call.

Attachments: redwood-data-questions-brief.pdf (questionnaire)

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen

Thanks Stephanie — that recap is accurate. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Retention: Production must support 90 days of telemetry retention by default for our audit needs. We can keep staging shorter.
2) Subprocessors: we need a full current list and a commitment to notify changes 30 days prior.
3) Breach timeline: our security team expects initial notification within 48 hours of confirming a breach that impacts our data. An acknowledgement of an incident within 24 hours is acceptable, but substantive notification needs to be 48 hours for PII incidents.
4) Logs: we cannot receive full raw PII in logs; redacted exports or hashed identifiers are acceptable for investigations.

I attached our internal requirements doc (TH_Data_Requirements_v2.docx) — it contains sample DPA language and the specific fields we consider PII.

Hi Jake / Anna — thanks for the clear doc and call earlier this week. Apologies for the slightly long note below — wanted to give explicit answers so your procurement/legal folks have language to work with.

1) Controller vs Processor
- Default position: Redwood acts as a Processor when we are processing data strictly per a customer’s instructions for hosted and Dedicated offerings. The customer (TerraHeal) remains the Controller for customer-supplied PII.
- Alternate arrangements: For some integration patterns (where Redwood enriches or routes data for other downstream services), we can review and include tailored language.

Proposed clause (short): “Redwood Inference shall process Customer Data only on the Controller’s documented instructions. For the avoidance of doubt, Customer remains the Controller of Customer Data; Redwood is a Processor except where otherwise agreed in writing.”

2) Subprocessors & notification
- We maintain a current subprocessor registry here: https://redwood.ai/legal/subprocessors (attached CSV).
- We can commit to notifying TerraHeal of changes to the subprocessor list at least 30 days in advance for non‑emergency additions. For emergency additions required to address security or availability incidents, we will notify as soon as practicable and provide alternative mitigation options.

3) Breach / incident notification timeline
- Acknowledgement: Redwood will acknowledge receipt of a suspected security incident within 24 hours of detection.
- Initial notification: For confirmed incidents that materially affect Customer Data (including PII), Redwood will provide an initial incident notification within 72 hours of confirmation.
- Expedited notification for PII compromises: where we confirm unauthorized access to PII, Redwood agrees to provide an initial notification within 48 hours of confirmation.
- Root cause & remediation: Redwood will share a substantive incident report and remediation plan within 30 days, with status updates until closure.

Note: the distinction is detection vs confirmation — we can acknowledge quickly on detection, but our timelines for the initial substantive notification are tied to confirmation so that we do not provide inaccurate or incomplete information.

4) Logs & PII
- We collect application logs and inference metadata. We do not provide raw customer PII as part of standard log exports. Where necessary for investigations, we can produce redacted exports or hashed identifiers under an NDA/secure transfer.
- Retention: Hosted default retention for logs is 30 days. For production workloads we can offer configurable retention up to 90 days on Dedicated or via a Private deployment.

5) Data residency
- Redwood supports region pinning for model execution in EU and US regions on Hosted (region-available models) and Dedicated/Private deployments for stronger residency guarantees. We’ll document the exact region mapping for your planned deployment in the next email.

Attachments: subprocessors_2026-11.csv

If any of the above needs tighter SLA language or a different timeline, happy to iterate. Stephanie — once you confirm TerraHeal is ok with the 72/48 distinction above, I’ll convert the bullets into contract-ready wording for the DPA addendum.

Regards,
Monica Patel
